```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4, dpi = 110)
options(tibble.print_min = 6, width = 90)
```

Since 2023-24 the NHL has kept the puck and player tracking behind every goal: about fourteen seconds
of every skater, both goalies and the puck, ten frames a second. NHL.com uses it for its goal replays.
This vignette reads one goal end to end, Connor McDavid's shorthanded breakaway at Boston on
18 December 2025, from the copy that ships with the package, so nothing here needs the network.
`nhl_goal_tracking(2025020534, 777)` fetches the same frames.

```{r}
library(bluelineR)
path <- system.file("extdata", "goal-2025020534-777.json.gz", package = "bluelineR")
frames <- read_goal_tracking(path, game_id = 2025020534, event_id = 777)
frames
```

Each row is one object in one frame. `x` runs along the rink and `y` across it, in feet from centre
ice, the frame the play-by-play uses: the nets are at x = -89 and +89. The puck is `entity_id` 1.

## When it went in

The clip runs on past the goal, and the puck can sit at the other net when it starts or blip over the
line before the real goal. `goal_frame()` wants it in the net, between the posts, two frames running,
at the net the clip finishes at:

```{r}
g <- goal_frame(frames)
g
frames[frames$frame == g & frames$is_puck, c("time", "x", "y")]
```

## How it was scored

```{r}
goal <- classify_goal(frames, team = "EDM", shot_type = "backhand")
t(goal[, c("shooter", "distance", "shot_speed", "since_neutral", "passes", "rush", "breakaway",
           "oddman", "onetimer", "cross", "traffic", "behind", "forecheck")])
```

It was a rush (the puck was in Edmonton's end 2.8 seconds before the shot) and a breakaway: McDavid
carried it over the blue line with no Bruin but the goalie between him and the net. He shot from
7.5 feet; the puck left his stick at 24 mph, a backhand.

The rules in `?classify_goal` are the ones BluelineMetrics builds its goal types with. On 120 goals from
2025-26 the R version agrees with the site's on every type, the shooter, the distance, the shot speed
and the number of passes.

## How fast he was going

`skater_speed()` gives every skater's speed at every frame, over the 0.6 seconds around it:

```{r}
speed <- skater_speed(frames)
mcd <- speed[speed$player_id == 8478402, ]
round(max(mcd$speed_mph, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
```

## Drawing it

```{r, fig.alt = "Every player's position as the puck goes in, with the last two seconds of each path."}
plot_goal(frames, title = "McDavid, shorthanded breakaway at Boston")
```

```{r, fig.height = 7, fig.alt = "Six frames over the five seconds before the goal."}
plot_goal_sequence(frames, n = 6, seconds = 5)
```

`nhl_rink()` is the empty rink, in the same feet, for drawing anything else on.
